albums.blurb: Blow by Blow was the first album the English guitarist released under his own name alone, after runs fronting the Yardbirds and the Jeff Beck Group. Recorded in late 1974 with Beatles producer George Martin and keyboardist Max Middleton, it drops rock vocals entirely for a set of jazz-funk instrumentals, including two Stevie Wonder compositions — among them "Cause We've Ended as Lovers," dedicated to guitarist Roy Buchanan.
albums.reception: It peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and was certified platinum by the RIAA, outselling every album Beck had made with the Jeff Beck Group and Beck, Bogert & Appice.

albums.blurb: Oscar Jerome is a south London guitarist and singer who came up through the city's jazz scene as a member of the Afrobeat-influenced band Kokoroko. Breathe Deep, his debut studio album, folds jazz guitar, neo-soul, funk and hip-hop together across eleven tracks, with contributions from Kokoroko bandmates, players from the Ezra Collective orbit, and singer Lianne La Havas.
albums.reception: Music Republic Magazine named it Album of the Month for August 2020, calling it "challenging but easy listening, totally fresh yet familiar."

albums.blurb: Rushen was a classically trained jazz pianist who cut three albums for Prestige while still in her early twenties before pivoting to R&B at Elektra. Straight from the Heart, her seventh album, was largely self-produced and yielded "Forget Me Nots" — whose bassline later resurfaced in Will Smith's "Men in Black" — alongside the oft-sampled "Remind Me" and the instrumental "Number One."
albums.reception: Her most successful album, it reached No. 14 on the Billboard 200 and earned her first two Grammy nominations, for "Forget Me Nots" (Best Female R&B Vocal Performance) and "Number One" (Best R&B Instrumental Performance).
